notes.text: Binary → Gray code, streamed: each output bit is the current input bit XOR the previous one. Gray code is the encoding where consecutive numbers differ in exactly ONE bit — used in rotary encoders and error-resistant hardware.
Two states carry all the memory needed: which bit came before. Try 0111 (7) and 1000 (8) — their Gray codes 0100 and 1100 differ in a single bit, even though the binary inputs differ in all four.

meta.title: Binary → Gray code
meta.blurb: Streams a binary number into its Gray code (output = bit XOR previous bit). Adjacent values end up differing in exactly one bit — the trick rotary encoders rely on.
